newsitem.title: USA: Radio sports announcer convicted in U.S. drug case.
newsitem.headline: Radio sports announcer convicted in U.S. drug case.

text.p: A federal jury took less than 30 minutes on Friday to find Julio Gonzalez, who announced San Francisco Giants baseball games in Spanish for a local radio station, guilty on five counts of drug trafficking and money laundering.
A native of Nicaragua, Gonzalez, 51, faces a sentence of between 10 years and life. Sentencing was scheduled for Sept. 5, U.S. Attorney Michael Yamaguchi said.

During the four-week trial, prosecutors alleged Gonzalez belonged to a group that distributed 220 pounds (100 kg) of cocaine in 1994 and laundered several hundred thousand dollars in drug proceeds to dealers in Los Angeles and Colombia.
Prosecutors said one of his partners was Jose Trimmino, a Colombian race car driver who in 1979 won the Marlboro Cup series. Trimmino, 55, pleaded guilty to conspiracy and money laundering charges.

Gonzalez, Trimmino and three co-defendants were arrested in June 1994. Cesar Diossa, 38, pleaded guilty and is awaiting sentencing, while Luis Torres, 29, awaits retrial. Bricio Morales, 32, Gonzalez's brother-in-law, fled after posting bail and remains at large.
